Hypotheses: 15 possible pairs × 2 rules = 30 possibilities. I'll start by testing half the objects to split them.

TEST: zekuror, nonogok, mikazak
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test failing leaves 15 possibilities:
- **If one nexiom is enough:** neither nexiom is among zekuror, nonogok, mikazak. So the pair is two of lonigos, sirimi, firomu (3 options).
- **If both nexioms are needed:** the pair is anything except a pair taken entirely from the first three objects (12 options).

Testing zekuror, nonogok, lonigos, sirimi splits these almost evenly:
- **It lights up (8 cases):** the one-nexiom rule with any of the 3 pairs among lonigos, sirimi, firomu. Or the two-nexiom rule with zekuror–lonigos, zekuror–sirimi, nonogok–lonigos, nonogok–sirimi or lonigos–sirimi.
- **It stays dark (7 cases):** the two-nexiom rule with zekuror–firomu, nonogok–firomu, mikazak–lonigos, mikazak–sirimi, mikazak–firomu, lonigos–firomu or sirimi–firomu.

TEST: zekuror, nonogok, lonigos, sirimi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine must need **both nexioms**. Under the one-nexiom rule, the pair would have to come from lonigos, sirimi and firomu. Any such pair includes lonigos or sirimi, so the second test would have lit up.

Under the two-nexiom rule, 7 pairs remain: zekuror–firomu, nonogok–firomu, mikazak–lonigos, mikazak–sirimi, mikazak–firomu, lonigos–firomu and sirimi–firomu.

The next test, mikazak, firomu, lonigos, splits these 3 to 4:
- **It lights up (3 pairs):** mikazak–lonigos, mikazak–firomu or lonigos–firomu.
- **It stays dark (4 pairs):** zekuror–firomu, nonogok–firomu, mikazak–sirimi or sirimi–firomu.

Either group can be narrowed to one pair within the 3 tests left.

TEST: mikazak, firomu, lonigos
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine needs **both nexioms**, so a test lights up only if it contains the whole pair. The third test stayed dark, which leaves 4 possible pairs:
- zekuror–firomu
- nonogok–firomu
- mikazak–sirimi
- sirimi–firomu

The next test, zekuror, firomu, sirimi, splits these 2 to 2:
- **It lights up:** the pair is zekuror–firomu or sirimi–firomu.
- **It stays dark:** the pair is nonogok–firomu or mikazak–sirimi.

One more test will then settle which pair it is.

TEST: zekuror, firomu, sirimi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine needs **both nexioms**. The last test stayed dark, so the pair is either nonogok–firomu or mikazak–sirimi.

Testing nonogok and firomu together settles it:
- **It lights up:** the nexioms are nonogok and firomu.
- **It stays dark:** the nexioms are mikazak and sirimi.

TEST: nonogok, firomu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Nonogok and firomu together stayed dark, so the only pair left is **mikazak and sirimi**. It fits every result: no test contained both of them, so under the two-nexiom rule none of them could light up. The second test already ruled out the one-nexiom rule, so the machine **needs two**.

ANSWER: nexioms = mikazak, sirimi; needs = two

So 8 hypotheses predict "lit" and 7 predict "dark". A dark result would also eliminate the "one" rule completely.

The second test was dark too, so the rule must be **"two"**. Under "one", every surviving pair (from dadivel, futivun and rutazi) contained dadivel or futivun and would have lit it.

- **Dark:** the pair is bavonak–rutazi, sugudik–rutazi, zabale–futivun or futivun–rutazi.

Either way, at most 4 pairs remain, which 2 more tests can settle. That leaves 1 test to spare.

Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The third test was dark, so I can remove zabale–dadivel, zabale–rutazi and dadivel–rutazi. The rule is still "two", and 4 pairs remain:

- **Dark:** the pair is sugudik–rutazi or zabale–futivun.

One more test after this will settle it, which leaves 1 test to spare.

TEST: bavonak, futivun, rutazi
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The fourth test lit up, so the pair is inside {bavonak, futivun, rutazi}. The rule is still "two", and only 2 pairs remain:
- bavonak–rutazi
- futivun–rutazi

Next I'll test {bavonak, rutazi}:
- **Lit:** the pair is bavonak–rutazi.
- **Dark:** the pair is futivun–rutazi.

This settles it, with 1 test to spare.

TEST: bavonak, rutazi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The fifth test was dark, so the pair is not bavonak–rutazi. The only remaining pair is **futivun–rutazi**.

All five results fit this pair under the "two" rule:
- **Test 1 (bavonak, sugudik, zabale):** dark, since neither nexiom was on.
- **Test 2 (bavonak, sugudik, dadivel, futivun):** dark, since futivun was there but rutazi was not.
